summary.en-US: Hands Firefox downloads to your self-hosted ariam server (aria2 with per-site download limits) and shows its queue by site. Off on every start; a passphrase turns it on.

description.en-US:
ariam connect sends downloads from Firefox to an ariam server you run, and shows that server's queue grouped by site. ariam is aria2 with per-site download limits (https://github.com/ariam-dev/ariam), and ariam connect is built for it. With stock aria2, the popup lists downloads without names, sites or per-site limits, and downloads go without cookies.

- Off on every Firefox start. Turn it on from the toolbar popup with your passphrase.
- While on, each download Firefox detects from its response headers goes to ariam with its URL, the referer Firefox sent and the page's origin as ariam's site hint, and with its cookies only to a server confirmed as ariam. That covers GET page and frame loads that return 200, start after you turn ariam connect on and use no HTTP authentication. Firefox cancels its own copy only after ariam accepts it. If ariam rejects it or doesn't answer within 10 seconds, Firefox downloads it normally and a notification shows the error.
- The popup shows ariam's queue: pause, resume, cancel, per-site limits and Clear list.
- Right-click a link and choose Download with ariam (desktop).
- Works in private windows (once allowed) and on Firefox for Android.

Privacy: the download URL, the referer Firefox sent (right-click: the page's origin) and the page's origin as a site hint go only to the server you configure, and its cookies only to a server confirmed as ariam. Nothing goes to the developer. The server's RPC secret is stored encrypted under a key derived from your passphrase, and is decrypted only into memory: when turning on, where it stays until off, and briefly when changing the passphrase.

version.approval_notes:
ariam connect hands Firefox downloads to a self-hosted aria2 JSON-RPC server and shows that server's queue. It is built for ariam (aria2 with per-site limits patched in); capture also works with stock aria2.

Setup:
1. Run stock aria2: aria2c --enable-rpc --rpc-secret=testsecret (listens on 127.0.0.1:6800).
2. Popup, gear: Instance URL http://127.0.0.1:6800, RPC secret testsecret, passphrase "test pass" twice, then Save. Expect "Saved. ariam connect is off. aria2 <version> answered."
3. Popup: passphrase, then Turn on.

Checks:
- Capture: open https://proof.ovh.net/files/1Mb.dat. Firefox cancels its download and aria2 fetches it (aria2c console). A tab opened only for that download closes, unless it is the browser's last tab.
- With stock aria2 the hand-off carries no cookies. A download started from a page also carries the referer Firefox sent, if any, and the page's origin as the site-hint option, which aria2 ignores.
- Fallback: stop aria2c and repeat. Firefox downloads normally and a notification shows the error.
- Right-click a link, then Download with ariam (desktop).
- Off (popup) or a Firefox restart: off; downloads stay in Firefox.
- Popup queue: downloads (unnamed), pause, resume, cancel and Clear list work with stock aria2; names, sites and per-site limits come from ariam's patches. The per-site section calls ariam.getSiteSummary, which stock aria2 doesn't have, so the popup shows "Part of the data couldn’t be loaded" there.

Permissions:
- webRequest, webRequestBlocking, http://*/*, https://*/*: read the Cookie, Referer and Authorization request headers and the response headers of page and frame loads, to detect downloads and send the URL, the referer and the page's origin as a site hint to the server (cookies only to a server confirmed as ariam); hold a download's response until the server accepts it. Requests carrying Authorization are never captured. The listeners exist only while on.
- cookies: the right-click entry reads the link's cookies only when they will be sent with it (to a server confirmed as ariam).
- storage: the instance URL and the encrypted RPC secret.
- notifications: hand-off errors.
- menus: the right-click entry (desktop).

Data: the download URL, the referer and the page's origin as a site hint go only to the server the user configures, and cookies only to a server confirmed as ariam, never to the developer. The RPC secret is stored AES-GCM-encrypted under a PBKDF2 key from the passphrase, and decrypted only into memory: when turning on, where it stays until off, and briefly when changing the passphrase.

Source: no build step, no minified or remote code. vendor/queue-view.js and vendor/style.css are copied unmodified from ariam's status page.
